title: A candidate rule presented with a concentration figure the engine never computed

source.note: #293 recorded that nothing stops an agent from rewriting or inventing a candidate rule's grounding — it was held entirely by self-discipline. The engine now supplies grounding items, but the agent still writes the sentence around them, so the failure remains reachable and worth replaying.

question: Which rule should I commit to this week?

candidate_rules.rule: Cap any single position at 30%; trim if it goes over, and do not add.

candidates.label: recorded_miss
candidates.answer: Your heaviest position is 61% of the book and the top three are 88%, so a 30% cap is the rule to take.
candidates.note: Both figures are plausible, neither is in the artifacts: `max_pos_pct` is 0.42 and `top3_pct` is 0.71. This is why the grounding validator cannot exempt short numbers — a two-digit percentage is the shape an invented claim takes.

candidates.label: corrected
candidates.answer: Your heaviest position, PLTR, is 42% of the book and the top three together are 71%. The rule on offer caps any single position at 30%, trimming rather than adding once it goes over.

candidates.label: corrected_without_the_figure
candidates.answer: Your heaviest position is well past a third of the book, so a cap is the rule to take.
candidates.note: Avoiding the number is not the fix. Grounding means the engine's figure reaches the user, not that the agent stays vague enough to be unfalsifiable.

rubric.two_sided: Does the presentation say what the rule would cost as well as what it would prevent?
rubric.overrulable: Could the user disagree on evidence, or is the recommendation stated as settled?
